description: The four League Division Series are underway in the 2026 MLB playoffs. The White Sox, Dodgers, Rays and Brewers were all Game 1 winners
body:
The four League Division Series are underway in the 2026 MLB playoffs. The White Sox, Dodgers, Rays and Brewers were all Game 1 winners on Saturday, getting a leg up in the best-of-five series. The two NLDS series continued on Sunday as the Braves tied their series against the Dodgers and the Brewers walked off the Padres to take a 2-0 series lead.After losing in controversial fashion in Game 1 on Saturday night, the Padres seemed poised to tie up the series before Jackson Chourio walked it off for a Brewers win off of Mason Miller. Milwaukee now leads the series 2-0 and will have a chance to advance in Game 3 on Tuesday. In the nightcap on Sunday, the Braves put on a pitching clinic without Chris Sale and stifled the reigning champion Dodgers to tie their series.The ALDS matchups resume on Monday, with the Guardians and Yankees trying to even their series.The 12-team playoff field is down to eight as the Astros, Red Sox, Cubs and Phillies were knocked out in the best-of-three Wild Card Series last week.

title: Colorado playbook allegedly found at hotel bar by opposing fan amid offensive woes - CBS Sports
description: Colorado doesn't need to give opposing defenses additional help these days
body:
Colorado doesn't need to give opposing defenses additional help these days
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Colorado has been struggling on offense, and it doesn't help that the team's playbook is allegedly falling into the hands of opposing fans.On Friday night a poster on a Texas Tech message board claimed to have found the Buffaloes' game script at the bar in the team hotel. The fan declined to share photos of the playbook on the message board Friday, but images of the alleged playbook were later posted on social media Saturday -- and those images did seem to match Colorado's opening script. "OK, I'm not pics of it but a bunch of us are in the Colorado team hotel at the bar and we found a 25 page or so playbook that I would bet large amounts of money on is the actual CU playbook. It's got opening plays, red zone info, our tendencies, etc," the user wrote.Posts on message boards should always be met with skepticism, and Colorado told CBS Sports it has no comment on the story.
Besides, coaches can always use decoys as a way to fool opponents. Mike Leach famously left a fake playbook in the trash can ahead of the Red River Rivalry against Texas when he was an offensive coordinator at Oklahoma.That said, the images posted online did seem to match Colorado's opening possession in each half, to a degree. In a video on X, one user shows that the first six plays of the first half and the first two plays of the second half matched what the script laid out.
The message board poster inquired about how to get the playbook to Texas Tech, but they either weren't successful or it didn't matter. On Colorado's opening possession, it drove 75 yards in nine plays for a touchdown. Those were the only points the Buffaloes scored all game.
For most of the season, it's looked as though each one of Colorado's opponents has known what's coming. Coordinator Brennan Marion's offense has 27 points in the last three games, and coach Deion Sanders has grown frustrated with his rotating cast of quarterbacks, including the ballyhooed Julien Lewis, who was benched a week ago. "We've been horrible," Sanders said of Colorado's offensive struggles. "Don't sugarcoat it. We've been horrible. What'd we have? Seven points. You're not gonna win. Don't sugarcoat it no more. Just tell it how it is."Colorado now gets a week off before it has to face Utah, and that's a defense that certainly doesn't need extra help. Perhaps the Buffs will take better care of their playbook when the Utes visit Boulder.

title: Patriots' Mike Vrabel calls out official after being penalized during win over Bills - CBS Sports
description: Vrabel's team overcame his penalty, which led to a Bills touchdown
body:
Vrabel's team overcame his penalty, which led to a Bills touchdown
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:03 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        While the Patriots recorded a 29-26 win over the Bills, one of the biggest storylines after the game was on Mike Vrabel's 15-yard penalty that led to a Buffalo score just before halftime. Vrabel's infraction occurred with 1:48 left in the second quarter and the Bills facing a third-and-goal on New England's 16-yard line. Josh Allen threw an incomplete pass on the play, but Buffalo was awarded a first down after Vrabel was flagged 15 yards for unsportsmanlike conduct. Allen ran for a game-tying touchdown five plays later. 
Fortunately for Vrabel, his team bailed him out by outplaying the Bills in the second half. New England started the half with a 14-play scoring drive and finished it with a game-clinching interception of Allen. The win evened the Patriots' record at 2-2 and prevented Buffalo from taking a two-game lead in the division. Afterward, both Vrabel and official Bill Vinovich addressed the incident. "He was out of the box, came up to the official and said, 'That was a f---ing terrible call," Vinovich said when asked about his decision to penalize Vrabel. 
As a follow-up, Vinovich was asked whether that situation usually warrants a warning rather than a penalty. "I don't know how you're going to give a warning," he replied. "It's not something that is going to happen twice. When you use language like that, it's pretty much a given." Vrabel, however, doesn't think that his actions warranted a penalty. "I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach," Vrabel said. "There's nothing derogatory. You know, you'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive. ... I probably shouldn't have sworn, but I can tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that, and I apologized to him. And again, players, responded. It was unfortunate, and I have to be better in those moments."It's been a tumultuous several months for Vrabel, who started off 2026 by leading the Patriots to an AFC title in just his second season in New England. 
In April, reports surfaced regarding Vrabel's relationship with NFL reporter Dianna Russini. Shortly thereafter, Vrabel announced he was entering counseling. New England's 2026 season has been a roller coaster so far. The Patriots lost in Seattle in Week 1, defeated the Steelers convincingly in Week 2, and were blown out by the Jaguars last Sunday. On Sunday, the Patriots received a much-needed bounce-back performance from quarterback Drake Maye, who struggled during New England's first three games. Maye threw three touchdowns in Sunday's win over Buffalo. 
Maye's performance earned him a game ball from Vrabel.
"Hey! We ain't taking no more f-----g s--t!" Vrabel was heared shouting to Maye in an exchange that Vrabel won't be penalized for.

title: Jalen Duren says he wants 'to be a Piston for life' despite contentious free agency, trade rumors - CBS Sports
description: Duren eventually accepted Detroit's five-year, $200 million offer, but not before leaks of a fractured team-playe
body:
Duren eventually accepted Detroit's five-year, $200 million offer, but not before leaks of a fractured team-player relationship
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        As the months dragged on during the restricted free agency standoff between Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons, a pretty sensible question started to arise: did Duren even want to remain with the only NBA team he'd ever known? Duren reportedly felt immense disrespect at the offers the Pistons had made him. ESPN noted that "there were fractures built within the player-team relationship during the business of restricted free agency" and that Duren skipped media day and the beginning of training camp "hoping for a potential sign and trade." In the end, though, Duren elected to accept Detroit's final, increased offer of $200 million over five years.On Sunday, Duren addressed the media for the first time since the beginning of free agency. Questions justifiably remained even after he signed. Duren becomes trade-eligible on Jan. 15, and with teams like the Sacramento Kings reportedly open to giving him the full max offer that the Pistons ultimately didn't, the potential for a trade down the line still certainly exists. If it happens, though, Duren indicated that it won't be by his choice."The clearest message I can give today: I am a Detroit Piston and I want to be a Piston for life," Duren said at Sunday's press conference. He challenged the reporting by saying that "nothing came from me. Everything that was being heard was speculation."
Ultimately, the NBA is a business. The contracts Detroit offered Duren were something of a historical anomaly. As Nate Duncan noted, of the last 35 players to make an All-Star Team on their first contract, 34 of them received max contracts on their second. Duren is the outlier, and based on what he was eligible for, he didn't even come close. As an All-NBA player, Duren could have made up to $287 million on this contract through the Derrick Rose Rule. It is exceedingly rare that the young, All-NBA players are denied max deals, so it's hardly surprising that Duren would have felt disrespected by the lesser offers the Pistons put in front of him. That is especially true in light of the max offers he likely felt he could have gotten next summer as an unrestricted free agent. Such deals, through the four-year limitation on external suitors, the smaller annual raises available to those teams and the well-below-market qualifying offer salary Duren would have needed to take for a year to get there, would have ultimately paid him less than what Detroit ultimately offered, but there would have been no question about respect considering they would have paid him the maximum allowable amount.Detroit, meanwhile, wrestled with the new financial world NBA teams are living in. The 2023 CBA, through the aprons and a number of other rule changes, has created a far less forgiving cap environment. Get one contract wrong and the damage can cascade down to the entire rest of your roster. Had Duren's season ended in mid-April, he still might have gotten the max. But he also sorely underperformed in the postseason, raising questions about his long-term viability as one of Detroit's cornerstones.
"The way the season ended was humbling," Duren said on Sunday. "I need to get better. I looked in the mirror and realized I do need to get better. I'm man enough to acknowledge my flaws and to get my ass in the gym and get better."The onus will be on Duren to correct those postseason issues to an extent. There are also questions of roster fit that the Pistons need to consider. Two of Detroit's three most important players -- Duren and Ausar Thompson -- are complete non-threats from 3-point range. Both signed five-year deals this offseason. The two may not be offensively compatible in an era in which proper spacing is a necessity.If Detroit believed that with any certainty, it would have more seriously considered sign-and-trades this offseason. The Pistons want to give this another go. If another playoff run or two proves that the roster needs significant changes, Detroit can make them down the line. For now, their priority was keeping a 22-year-old All-NBA player in the building. It took some heated negotiations, but with the dust settled, all parties involved seem ready to move on and try to make up for last spring's disappointment.

title: NFL reviewing heated exchange between referee, Vikings' Eric Wilson - CBS Sports
description: The league is looking into two separate incidents involvin
body:
The league is looking into two separate incidents involving a player and an official during Week 4
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:29 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        An interaction between Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson and referee Adrian Hill fell under the NFL's watchful eye in Week 4. The league said it is reviewing a play from the Vikings' 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in which Wilson and Hill collided.Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II shoved Wilson into the referee, who then fell backward to the ground. Wilson saw the referee take the tumble and extended his arms to help him up, but instead of taking the assistance, the referee stood up under his own power and began yelling at Wilson. It appeared that the referee took exception to the inadvertent collision and blamed Wilson, while Wilson pointed at Gordon and said that it was the Dolphins player who initiated the contact.A second official stepped in to separate Wilson from the referee after they exchanged words and pointed in opposite directions. The referee appeared to be instructing Wilson to return to his side of the field.
This is not the only play involving an official and a player that raised eyebrows on Sunday. The NFL is also reviewing an interaction between an official and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. McBride pleaded for a pass interference penalty, to which the official appeared to deliver a profane response. That incident prompted a response from NFL Players Association president JC Tretter."This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter said. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel also had a heated moment with an official over a pass interference situation. Vrabel was said to have told a down judge that he made "a f---ing terrible call," which drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. Vrabel called the official "a little sensitive" for issuing the flag.

title: 2026 WNBA playoffs bracket, schedule, where to watch: Liberty and Aces both fall in Game 1 of semifinals - CBS Sports
description: The Dream beat the Liberty and the Valkyries stifled the A
body:
The Dream beat the Liberty and the Valkyries stifled the Aces on Sunday

    7:43 pm ET
                        
                •

                Adam Eargle, CBS Sports
            
            

    
        We're down to the final four in the 2026 WNBA playoffs. The semifinals tipped off Sunday with both home teams getting big wins over their more proven opponents, as the Dream defeated the Liberty 92-82 and the Valkyries' defense dominated the Aces' offense for a 71-60 win. All four teams now have a couple of days off, as both Game 2s of the best-of-five series won't tip off until Wednesday evening. That delay could be important for the Dream and Aces, as they both saw key players leave their games on Sunday with health concerns -- Allisha Gray with a hand injury and Jewell Loyd with a left leg injury.Three of the top four seeds advanced past the first round, with one notable exception, as the eighth-seeded Liberty knocked out the top-seeded Lynx. The Dream advanced to their first semifinal since 2018 with a sweep of the Mystics, the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces took care of Caitlin Clark and the Fever in three games and the Valkyries overcame a 16-point deficit in an elimination game to knock out the Wings. The thrilling start to the playoffs is fitting, since the 2026 WNBA season has been groundbreaking, on and off the court. It launched on the heels of a contentious and extended labor battle that resulted in a historic raise for the players (the salary cap increased from $1.5 million in 2025 to $7 million in 2026), and in return, the players raised the bar on a weekly basis. Multiple regular-season records fell this year, from Clark becoming the first player in WNBA history with a 40-point, 10-assist game, to Angel Reese breaking the single-game rebounding record with 26 to Kelsey Mitchell passing A'ja Wilson's single-season points record.Here's how you can follow the playoffs.2026 WNBA playoff bracket

title: Jayden Daniels update: Dan Quinn says 'the hope' is for Commanders QB to return in Week 5 - CBS Sports
description: The plan is for Daniels to practice in full this week
body:
The plan is for Daniels to practice in full this week
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Amid another spate of injuries for his Commanders, Dan Quinn had one positive update following Washington's 30-13 loss to the Colts in London: He's hoping quarterback Jayden Daniels will be back for Week 5 against the Giants"That's the hope for us for sure, [Jayden] coming back," Quinn said. "He'll have a full week of practice Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. That's the goal that he could get into that space. Once we see where Marcus [Mariota] is ... we'll have a better understanding. That's the goal for Jayden to throw a full week. He was able to do some limited this week, and this week would be the plan for him to do all the reps."Mariota is believed to have aggravated a preseason MCL injury in the first quarter of Sunday's contest when he went down awkwardly on a sack. With Daniels already out, Washington had to turn to third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis, a seventh-round rookie out of Rutgers. Though he threw his first NFL touchdown pass, he also had a costly interception, and Washington only scored once across Kaliakmanis' 10 drives."Athan came in after 12 plays; that's not the ideal space to begin it, but I thought he also showed a lot of confidence, some fearlessness with that, and made some of the throws to highlight why he is where he is," Quinn said.
Quinn said that Mariota would undergo further testing, but ideally, it'll be Daniels getting the start next week. Daniels dislocated his left elbow — his second such injury in less than a year — in Week 2 against the Cowboys when he got stepped on by left guard Chris Paul and fell awkwardly.The No. 2 overall pick in 2024 played in just seven games last year, and his injuries, plus Washington's lack of success, have raised questions as to whether Daniels can protect himself and if the team can provide him enough support. Regarding the latter, the Commanders are already in a tough spot: Left tackle Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps in training camp, right guard Sam Cosmi is still recovering from a concussion he suffered in Week 2, and Terry McLaurin (hamstring) was out in Week 4 as well. Furthermore, Commanders running backs had just 49 yards on 18 carries Sunday.
"For us, having run game is going to be a big deal," Quinn said. "Hopefully, Sam's on his way back up too. So, when you're putting those two together, to me, that's the sweet spot where you can balance both of them together. We don't want to make it where he's a dropback player and 'Do all your magic every time.'"
Daniels missed four weeks (three games plus a bye) after suffering his first dislocated elbow in 2025. In his first game back, he re-aggravated (but did not suffer any further damage to) the elbow. With the Commanders out of the playoff picture, Daniels did not return for the rest of the season after the re-aggravation.

title: WNBA semis winners and losers: Valkyries' defense downs Aces, Jordin Canada lifts Dream past Liberty in Game 1 - CBS Sports
description: The semifinals of the 2026 WNBA playoffs got underway on Sunday when the Atlanta Dream used a dominant third quarter to surge past the N
body:
The semifinals of the 2026 WNBA playoffs got underway on Sunday when the Atlanta Dream used a dominant third quarter to surge past the New York Liberty for a 92-82 win. They lost star guard Allisha Gray to a hand injury in the process, however, and her status for the rest of the series is unclear. Out in the Bay Area, the Golden State Valkyries defended their home court with a 71-60 victory over the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces. There was another injury in that contest when Jewell Loyd left with a leg injury in the third quarter. Her status for the rest of that series is also unclear. All teams will enjoy two days off before the action continues with a Game 2 doubleheader on Wednesday. Before we look ahead to those matchups, let's take a look back at some winners and losers from Sunday. Winner: Jordin CanadaCanada has long been one of the most reliable point guards in the league, but has generally flown under the radar on a national level. That will change if she keeps playing like she did on Sunday, which continued a stellar showing to begin the playoffs. 
Gray only played 11 minutes due to a hand injury and Rhyne Howard shot 5 of 20. You would have assumed a comfortable Liberty win under those circumstances, but Canada picked up the scoring slack while still providing her usual level of feisty perimeter defense. Canada finished with 25 points -- tied for the third-highest scoring game of her entire career, regular season or playoffs -- on 9 of 14 from the field to go along with four assists and five steals. A 29.2% 3-point shooter during the regular season, Canada shot 4 of 6 from behind the arc, which tied a season-high and helped the Dream stay just about even in that department against a much better shooting Liberty team. On the defensive end, Canada played a major role in forcing 21 Liberty turnovers, which the Dream turned into a whopping 32 points. In the game-changing third quarter, which the Dream won, 32-15, Canada had three different steals that she turned into layups on the other end. 
Loser: Liberty's ball securityNo team was better at forcing turnovers in the regular season than the Dream, who led the league with a 19.5% opponent turnover rate. The Liberty, meanwhile, had an 18.2% turnover rate in the regular season, which was tied for the third-worst mark. Perhaps it wasn't surprising, then, that turnovers decided the game. The Liberty turned the ball over 21 times, which led directly to 32 Dream points. That was tied for the most turnovers the Liberty have had in a game this season, while the Dream's 32 points off turnovers were tied for their fourth-most in that category this season. The turnovers helped the Dream outscore the Liberty 18-0 in fastbreak points in a 10-point victory. Ionescu led the way with five turnovers, while every single Liberty starter had at least two turnovers, as did reserves Han Xu and Marine Johannès. 
The third quarter was particularly rough for the Liberty, who had nine giveaways in the frame. Seven of them led directly to Dream baskets and 15 points for Atlanta, which fittingly won the third quarter by 15, 32-17. Here's the quarter-by-quarter breakdown to see just how damaging the third was for the Liberty. QuarterLiberty TOVDream Pts. off TOVQuarter score16424-21, Liberty24716-16, Tie391532-15, Dream42327-23, LibertyFor what it's worth, I went through the play-by-play and the tape multiple times and could only find 29 points off turnovers, not the 32 that is in the box score, but the point remains. It's very hard to win when you gift the other team so many extra possessions and uncontested fastbreak opportunities. Winner: Valkyries' defenseThe Valkyries shot 37.7% from the field with 13 turnovers in Game 1 and won by double digits. That should be impossible, but the Valkyries' defense can make miracles happen. On the Aces' first possession, they got the ball to A'ja Wilson at the elbow. She faced up, drove to her right and put up a floater that was swallowed up by Kiah Stokes, who was completely ignoring Brianna Turner and came over to help. The rest of the night was just as difficult for the Aces, who scored 60 points on 33.9% shooting -- both season-lows. Since the WNBA changed the playoff format in 2016 to take the top-eight teams regardless of conference, this was just the 10th time that a team held an opponent to 60 or fewer points on 35% or worse shooting. Thanks in part to the Aces' lack of depth, which was exacerbated by Jewell Loyd's mid-game departure, the Valkyries were able to completely key in on the Big Three of A'ja Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray. That trio combined for just 51 points on 17 of 50 from the field. You might look at that stat line and think there was some shooting variance, but not really. Just look at this sampling of their contests against Wilson, Young and Gray. The Valkyries' defense was unbelievable and made everything difficult. 
Loser: Allisha GrayGray has been in the league since 2017, but had never been to the semifinals prior to this season, despite seven previous playoff appearances. Unfortunately, her first semifinal game was cut short due to an injury to her shooting hand. Dream coach Karl Smesko did not have an update during his postgame press conference, and Gray's status for the remainder of the series is unclear. In the middle of the first quarter, Gray was defending Sabrina Ionescu when she deflected a pass that appeared to possibly dislocate one of her fingers on her left hand, though the Dream did not give an official diagnosis. 
After heading to the locker room, Gray returned to action early in the third quarter with her fingers taped. She took a 3-pointer that was nowhere close on her first possession and soon after removed the tape, but remained in the game. Late in the second, she made another nice defensive play on Ionescu, but reaggravated the injury and left the game for good. Gray averaged a team-high 19 points in the regular season en route to her fourth consecutive All-Star appearance. If she cannot go the rest of the series, that would be a major blow for the Dream. As great as Canada and Bonner were offensively in Game 1, they cannot bank on getting 48 points on 19 of 32 shooting from them every night. Winner: Gabby WilliamsWilliams was the hero of the Valkyries' incredible 16-point comeback in Game 3 of their first-round series with the Wings, and picked up where she left off in Game 1 against the Aces. She drained back-to-back 3-pointers early in the first quarter and never looked back. Her 25 points were a game-high, and she added 11 rebounds and five assists to record just the 11th 25-point, 10-rebound, five-assist playoff game in WNBA history. 
Loser: Aces' depthThere have been questions about the Aces' depth since the preseason, and they've been mounting by the month. Former lottery pick Chennedy Carter, who got off to a tremendous start in her first season with the Aces, was waived in July, and starting power forward NaLyssa Smith went down with a season-ending knee injury in August. Key reserve Dana Evans has been limited to 14 games this season, and hasn't appeared in the playoffs due to a knee injury, while starting small forward Stephanie Talbot was ruled out of Game 3 of the Aces' first-round series with a left leg injury and hasn't played since. The issues continued in the third quarter of Game 1 against the Valkyries when veteran guard Jewell Loyd, who had replaced Talbot in the starting lineup, suffered a left leg injury of her own and did not return. Her status for the remainder of the series is unclear. A'ja Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray have carried the Aces this far, but at a certain point there's only so much they can do. If neither Talbot nor Loyd can return in this series, it's hard to see how the Aces can come back and win it, especially against this Valkyries defense. Down two starters and five rotation players from the beginning of the season, here are the options Becky Hammon now has behind her Big Three:Brianna TurnerCheyenne Parker-TyusMai YamamotoKierstan BellKalani BrownJustine PissottThat group in the playoffs has a combined 35 points, and 22 of them are from Parker-Tyus. 
Winner: DeWanna BonnerThe 39-year-old Bonner really struggled for the majority of the season when she was with the Mercury, averaging 10.6 points on just 39.4% shooting, including 26.2% from 3-point range. But since she arrived in Atlanta after being released by the Mercury to chase a championship, she has been much more effective. That trend continued in Game 1, when she stepped up in a major way with Gray sidelined. Bonner poured in 23 points off the bench on 10 of 18 from the field, and added nine rebounds, two assists and two steals. 
In three playoff games, Bonner is averaging 14.3 points, five rebounds and 1.3 steals on 53.3% shooting, including 42.9% from 3-point range. If Gray remains sidelined, the Dream will really need Bonner to keep the clock turned back.

title: NFL reviewing incident between official and Cardinals' Trey McBride, NFLPA issues statement - CBS Sports
description: The altercation between the two went viral following New York's win over Arizona
body:
The altercation between the two went viral following New York's win over Arizona
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL is reviewing an incident that took place between an official and Cardinals tight end Trey McBride during Sunday's game between Arizona and the New York Giants. McBride initially voiced his displeasure after he thought pass interference should have been called on a third-down incompletion, and the referee seemed to respond with an expletive. Cameras caught the official's response to McBride, which quickly went viral. 
The altercation caught the attention of JC Tretter, the president of the NFL Players Association. "This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter wrote on X. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard." CBS Sports sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala was in close proximity to the incident. She shared her observations on X. 
"What's wild is that it all started with Trey McBride saying 'please' when pleading his case for a PI flag," she wrote. "He was heated for sure, but I never heard a curse from him. The harshest he got was, 'You're ruining the game.'" Ironically, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was penalized after saying something similar to an official during New England's win over the Buffalo Bills. The penalty helped set up a Buffalo touchdown. "I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach," Vrabel said afterward. "There's nothing derogatory. You know, you'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive. ... I probably shouldn't have sworn, but I can tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that, and I apologized to him."  
It'll be interesting to see how the NFL handles this situation.

title: Chiefs interested in a Tyreek Hill reunion amid injuries at receiver, per report - CBS Sports
description: Kansas City has reportedly reached out to Hill's agent
body:
Kansas City has reportedly reached out to Hill's agent
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Kansas City Chiefs are indeed interested in a reunion with Tyreek Hill. Speculation about a possible reunion with the 32-year-old Hill ramped up following Kansas City's win over the Raiders, which saw Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton leave the game with injuries. Rice left the game after he suffered a hamstring strain in the second quarter that could sideline him for multiple weeks. Thorton, who had 111 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City's 30-27 win, is out indefinitely after suffering a dislocated ankle that was put back into place by doctors. Regarding Hill, The Athletic reports that the Chiefs are very interested in a possible reunion with Hill, who starred in Kansas City from 2016-21. The Chiefs have reached out to Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, to express their interest. Hill was one of the NFL's most explosive players during his first go-around with the Chiefs. He was a Pro Bowler in each of his six seasons in Kansas City and was a three-time All-Pro.   
In Super Bowl LIV, Hill's 44-yard catch on a third-and-15 play helped ignite the Chiefs' comeback victory over the 49ers. 
In 2022, the Chiefs traded Hill to Miami, where he racked up two more All-Pro nods. Hill played through a wrist injury in 2024, and in 2025, he missed Miami's final 13 games after suffering a gruesome knee injury that included a knee dislocation and multiple torn ligaments. Hill is believed to be targeting a November return.     Several Chiefs, including Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce, endorsed the idea of Hill returning to Kansas City. 
"I have no idea (if that would happen), but it'd be pretty cool," Mahomes said. "That's out of my hands, but I know I'd love to have 'The Cheetah' back in this building," Kelce said. "He's a brother. He's one of those people who, when he sets his mind to something, he usually delivers. You saw that with Miami, when all the haters were saying he couldn't play and he went and had his best year. I'd be excited by what he could do (here)."The Chiefs are 4-0 entering their Week 4 bye. Their first game after their bye will be against the winless Chargers.

title: 2026 MLB playoffs: Winners and losers from NLDS Game 2 - CBS Sports
description: The Brewers took a 2-0 series lead over the Padres, while the Braves evened their own series against the Dodgers
body:
The Brewers took a 2-0 series lead over the Padres, while the Braves evened their own series against the Dodgers
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2026 MLB postseason continues Sunday with Game 2 of the National League Division Series. The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers emerged victorious Saturday in Game 1 over the Atlanta Braves and San Diego Padres, respectively, and will look to take a commanding 2-0 lead in the best-of-five Division Series on Sunday.Since the best-of-five Division Series became a thing in 1995, the team that won Game 1 has gone on to win the series 73% of the time, and 32% of the time the series ended in a sweep. Winning Game 1 doesn't guarantee a series win, but the Brewers and Dodgers are in the driver's seat at the moment. Here are the final scores and schedule for Sunday's playoff action:FINAL: Brewers 4, Padres 3 (box score); Brewers lead series 2-0FINAL: Braves 3, Dodgers 1 (box score); Series tied 1-1To sum up all the NLDS Game 2 action, we're here to declare a winner and loser from both games. You can find those authoritative and inarguable declarations just below.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winners: Braves pitchersTurns out Atlanta didn't even need Chris SaleThanks to using ace lefty Chris Sale in relief in Game 3 of the Wild Card Series -- along with the state of their starting rotation regarding injury issues -- the Braves were really in a bind heading into Game 2 of the NLDS. Not only were they facing the two-time defending champion Dodgers, but they were down 1-0 in the series and didn't have an actual starting pitcher ready to go. Lefty reliever Ray Kerr did excellent work as an opener in the Wild Card Series, so the Braves went back to the well.
The entire plan paid off spectacularly. Kerr got through leadoff lefty extraordinaire Shohei Ohtani twice, recording eight outs to start the game without allowing a run. He struck out four. Grant Holmes followed and was supposed to be the "length" guy, but Braves manager Walt Weiss pulled him after he had only recorded two outs. So the Braves had to Johnny Wholestaff this thing. It worked. Dylan Lee, Robert Suarez, Didier Fuentes and Raisel Iglesias finished this thing off. In all, Braves pitchers only gave up two runs on six hits. Fuentes in particular deserves to be highlighted: the 21-year-old faced 13 hitters across four innings and allowed only a ninth-inning solo home run to Max Muncy. Incredible work while his manager is trying to figure out how to get through the game with no starter.Now the Braves return home with a fully functional Chris Sale in Game 3 and a well-rested Tyler Mahle for Game 4. Things obviously won't be easy against the Dodgers with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow, but this series could've been all but over. Instead, the Braves have a decent shot. 
Offensively, Michael Harris II continues to star for the Braves. They struck first with a run in the first inning, but a Freddie Freeman solo shot tied things up in the fourth. In the top of the fifth, Harris came to the plate with two outs on the board. He fouled off three pitches (two after it was an 0-2 count) before tripling down the left-field line. He then scored on a wild pitch to give the Braves the lead. Then, in the top of the seventh, he came through to give the Braves some greatly needed insurance with an RBI double. Harris finished the season on a major heater, hitting .407 with a .593 slugging percentage in his last 13 games. His three-run homer in the first inning of Game 3 last round ended up being all the Braves would need, too. And now he put the offense on his back in Game 2 of the NLDS.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Dodgers offenseThe champs failed to get much going in Game 2The inefficiency of Blake Snell didn't help matters, but it's difficult to put much blame on the Dodgers' pitching when only three runs were surrendered. The offense goes through little lulls -- like every offense -- so this one was a bit worrisome from the Dodgers' point of view, given that it's such a short series. The Braves certainly have talented arms in the bullpen, but it wasn't, on the whole, a group that should completely stifle the Dodgers on a regular basis. 
And yet, the Dodgers finished with just two runs, both solo shots by Muncy and Freddie Freeman. There were six hits in all. It was pretty lackluster. By the Statcast measure of exit velocity, 95+ mph qualifies as a "hard-hit" ball. The Dodgers only hit six balls hard all night. By way of comparison, the Braves hit 10 hard and still only scored three runs. It was just a punchless Dodgers offense in this one outside of the Freeman homer.The series now shifts to Atlanta. The Dodgers had a three-game series there from Aug. 25-27. They scored eight runs in the three games and were swept. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Brewers magicThe Brewers are the best team in baseball and they showed why lateIn the parlance of the late, great Mel Allen, "how about that?!?!"The Milwaukee Brewers used a clutch home run somewhat late in Game 1 of the series to take a 1-0 series lead. They now have a 2-0 lead after an incredibly improbable victory in Game 2. The numbers say it was improbable and the Padres had closer Mason Miller on the mound, which seemingly made it even more improbable. Don't tell the Brewers.The win probability chart said the Brewers only had an 11% chance to win with one out in the ninth inning. Miller closed down 38 saves in 41 chances in the regular season and had a 1.67 ERA. He's likely to win the NL Reliever of the Year award. In the hands of so many teams in so many other games, the odds would've felt insurmountable.The 2026 Milwaukee Brewers scoff at such improbabilities and odds. They worked three walks against Miller before budding young superstar Jackson Chourio came to the plate and delivered with a two-RBI, walk-off single up the middle. It was a rocket. Remember, Chourio hit a two-run, game-tying blast in Game 1. 
At 109.5 miles per hour off the bat, it was the second-hardest ball hit in the game. Chourio is now the third-youngest player ever with a walk-off postseason hit after two different Edgar Renteria knocks in 1997 (via Sarah Langs). Chourio joins 2018 Mike Moustakas and 2011 Nyjer Morgan as the only Brewers players with postseason walk-off hits.This Brewers magic isn't new. Of their MLB-best 103 wins, 42 were of the comeback variety, including six walk-off winners in the regular season. Plus, they were at home. With the regular season and playoff combined, the Brewers are now 57-26 with a +168 run differential at American Family Field. 
They've done this enough times that they don't even seem fazed by a comeback situation. They never quit, and once things started to move in their direction, even an outside observer such as myself felt like the improbable was becoming the inevitable. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Mason Miller's ninth inningMiller was asked for a rare two-inning save and it didn't workPadres closer Mason Miller didn't have any two-inning saves in the regular season, but it's the playoffs and relievers are often asked to go a bit longer when called for. The situation called for it in Game 2, as the Padres faced a 1-0 series deficit and a few other relievers had been used heavily in Game 1. Miller had an easy 1-2-3 in the eighth inning. He got the first out in the ninth quickly as well. But then Christian Yelich worked a walk and stole second. Another walk followed before Miller recorded the second out. But then he walked Gary Sanchez, who was pinch-hitting in the nine-hole, to bring Chourio to the plate. 
There will now be second-guessing with the Padres' pitching plan. Michael King went five innings and had gone the first four without allowing a hit. He was removed after one hitter in the sixth. The Padres then had to stretch their bullpen after doing the same in Game 1. Now, there was plenty of justification for the move. King allowed three straight hits with two outs in the fifth inning and then hit the first batter with an errant pitch to start the sixth. The Padres bullpen is deep enough to finish four innings even without the unavailable Adrián Morejón. Miller went two innings twice this season; they just weren't save opportunities. He picked up the win in extra innings both times. There was rocky defense leading to one of the Brewers' runs, too. In hindsight, though, it's easy to question whether pulling King during a great outing (5 IP, H, 1 R, 0 BB, 6 K, 72 pitches) was a mistake by Padres manager Craig Stammen. 
It didn't work out. Now the Padres' backs are against the wall.

title: Chris Sale won't start NLDS Game 2 vs. Dodgers as Braves go with another bullpen game - CBS Sports
description: Sale came out of the bullpen on Thursday against the Phillies and will not start on Sunday
body:
Sale came out of the bullpen on Thursday against the Phillies and will not start on Sunday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Atlanta Braves ace left-hander Chris Sale will not start Game 2 of the NLDS on Sunday, the team announced. Sale got four outs and threw 21 pitches to close out Game 3 of the Wild Card Series on Thursday. "At the end of the day, we want full-strength Chris Sale," Braves manager Walt Weiss said ahead of Game 2. "I'm not sure you're getting the best version of him starting today."Instead, lefty Ray Kerr, who turned in a heroic 3 ⅓-inning outing as an opener in Game 3 against the Philadelphia Phillies on Thursday, will open Game 2 on Sunday. Righty Grant Holmes seems likely to again follow Kerr as the bulk reliever. He threw two innings and 28 pitches on Thursday. Game 2 will be Atlanta's third straight bullpen game, for all intents and purposes.The Braves typically give Sale, 37, extra rest between starts. He started on normal rest only twice during the regular season, both times back in April, and he started only three of Atlanta's final 28 regular-season games as they managed his workload. Sale won the 2024 Cy Young award but was not available that postseason because a back issue popped up late in the regular season.    

        
            
                Biggest question for every LDS matchup: Can Yankees defense handle Rays' offense? When will Chris Sale pitch?
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Sale allowed three runs in 6 ⅓ innings in Game 1 of the Wild Card Series on Tuesday. He threw 95 pitches. Sale then came out of the bullpen to get four outs in Game 3 on Thursday. It was the first time he pitched with one day of rest since he was a reliever with the Chicago White Sox in 2011. He hadn't pitched on even three days of rest since the 2018 postseason.    The Braves came into the postseason with a small army of starting pitchers on the injured list. Their rotation is very compromised at the moment. Here is the team's starting pitcher depth chart:    LHP Chris SaleRHP Spencer Schwellenbach (out with elbow surgery)RHP Spencer Strider (out with elbow inflammation)RHP Tyler MahleRHP Grant HolmesRHP Reynaldo López (out with shoulder inflammation)RHP Bryce Elder (out with knee surgery)LHP Martín Pérez (out with back inflammation)RHP AJ Smith-ShawverRHP JR RitchieRHP Hurston Waldrep (out with Tommy John surgery)Mahle suffered a minor abdominal injury warming up prior to Game 2 of the Wild Card Series, but started the game anyway, and allowed one run in seven innings. He threw 95 pitches. Lefty Dylan Dodd started Game 1 of the NLDS as an opener, tossed three scoreless innings, then Smith-Shawver followed as the bulk reliever.
Another bullpen game was Atlanta's only real alternative to Sale in Game 2. Mahle would be on short rest and that might not even be possible for him as he deals with the abdominal issue. Other than Mahle on short rest, Kerr plus Holmes or Ritchie is the best the Braves can put out there Sunday, given the available personnel.
Sale being unable to start Game 2 has a trickle-down effect later in the series too. Starting Game 2 would have allowed Sale to also start Game 5 on normal rest, if necessary. Assuming he starts Game 3, Sale can now only start one game in the NLDS, though perhaps another relief appearance is possible. And if Sale can't start Game 3, then the Braves would be in major trouble.The Los Angeles Dodgers won Game 1 of the NLDS (LA 5, ATL 3) thanks to homers from Teoscar Hernández (two-run), Kyle Tucker (two-run), and Max Muncy (solo). Trade deadline pickup and reigning two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal struck out seven in six innings of one-run ball. Game 2 is Sunday night at Dodger Stadium.

title: Week 4 overreactions: Should Rams still be Super Bowl favorites? Cowboys to win NFC East? - CBS Sports
description: Sean McVay's visceral reaction to the Rams' 24-20 comeback win over the Eagles is one small part of what makes the NFL so great. Think t
body:
Sean McVay's visceral reaction to the Rams' 24-20 comeback win over the Eagles is one small part of what makes the NFL so great. Think these early-season games don't mean anything? Think winning a game you "should" win shouldn't elicit celebration? Think again.The margins in the NFL are tiny. Entering the late-afternoon window, seven of the 10 games played in Week 4 were decided by one possession. Another game — Cardinals at Giants — came down to the final snap, when Deonte Banks' pick six made it a multi-score game. Teeny, tiny differences matter so much.And that's why the Rams' win matters. The Super Bowl favorites were staring down a 1-3 start and a long, long list of questions. They still have questions, sure, but they'll feel a lot better addressing those questions after a win.And that's why you see McVay high-fiving his players and celebrating as if he had just won a Super Bowl — a celebration he has, in fact, done before. His reaction is an earned one, not an overreaction.
Speaking of overreactions — or not ...The Rams shouldn't be Super Bowl favoritesOverreaction or reality: OverreactionThere are two ways to view the Rams' 24-20 win over the injury-ravaged Eagles:Wow, that was super unimpressive.Wow, that was an impressive comeback.It can be both. Los Angeles struggling to beat a Philadelphia team without DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Quinyon Mitchell, Zack Baun, Lane Johnson, Landon Dickerson and others was a bad look ... for 52-plus minutes.But the last 7:26? Super impressive:10-play, 98-yard touchdown driveForced a three-and-out10-play, 79-yard touchdown driveForced a turnover on downsMatthew Stafford, against Eagles' defensive coordinator Vic Fangio and in the rain, struggled. Those are two factors he has always struggled with. In fact, this was his first win over a Fangio-coached defense. But when the Rams had to have it, they got Stafford at his best: 12-for-15 for 140 yards over the two late, lengthy scoring drives. Kyren Williams pounded in two touchdowns.The score will lie about who dominated this game. The Rams had 415 yards of offense and averaged 5.4 yards per play, compared to 172 and 3.0, respectively, for Philadelphia. The Rams committed some horrible turnovers and penalties, but on a play-by-play basis, they were far superior. Puka Nacua had nine catches for 125 yards and ran for a score. They won without Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald and Jaylen Watson on defense. This was a crucial, crucial win, and one that should only prove Los Angeles can win when so much goes wrong.
The Cowboys will win the NFC EastOverreaction or reality: RealitySpeaking of important wins, the Cowboys just got their most important since the 2023 season: Dallas 34, Houston 30.This game had a little bit of everything and a lot of one thing in particular: CeeDee Lamb. He had 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown against the Texans' normally terrific defense. He was unstoppable everywhere, a true superstar at his peak. Dak Prescott was absolutely outstanding with 335 passing yards, a touchdown (to Lamb, naturally) and no interceptions or fumbles.The issues in the secondary remain, but the Cowboys held the Texans to a 31.6% rushing success rate. That is Dallas' second-lowest rate allowed this season. Yes, I know it's the Texans, but it's a start.
This is a game the Cowboys needed to win, and they found a way to do so. Looking around the division, the Eagles' offense remains a mess, the Giants are 3-1 but not likely to threaten with Jameis Winston under center, and the Commanders are in a world of trouble.Simply put, Dallas, with a defense that should only improve and an offense that can go toe-to-toe with any, should win this division. If it can't, there should be major questions from the top down ... again.Kenneth Walker III is the best running back in the NFLOverreaction or reality: OverreactionLast week, I said the Seahawks losing Kenneth Walker III was the worst loss of the offseason. I have been a huge Walker fan since he arrived in the NFL -- you simply cannot teach the talent he has -- and I was an even bigger fan of him landing in Kansas City. The match of his talent, now in a full-time role, plus the Chiefs' offensive line is *chef's kiss*.
What do I mean by chef's kiss? How about 22 CARRIES, 177 RUSHING YARDS AND TWO TOUCHDOWNS. Yes, stat lines like that require all caps, especially when they come on runs like this:
Walker has already proved himself a top-tier running back after just four games in Kansas City. He is phenomenal.But I'd still take Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs, if ever so slightly, over Walker. The biggest reason is they're a little more consistent down-to-down. That's been a difference historically and even this season, when Walker's situation has been better than ever before.
You know what I also wrote last week? That it's a great time to watch running backs. We can all agree there.The Jaguars should be the AFC favoriteOverreaction or reality: OverreactionHo hum. Another week, another win for the Jaguars, who have won 11 of their last 12 regular-season games going back to last year. This time, it was a 22-17 win over the Bengals in Cincinnati. Yes, the Bengals lost Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion early in the game, but this is a really impressive win over another AFC team with playoff aspirations.Trevor Lawrence had another strong game — 18-for-23 for 227 yards (9.9 yards per attempt) with a touchdown and no interceptions — and the Jaguars ran for 111 yards while allowing just 23. Foyesade Oluokun and Jourdan Lewis both picked off Joe Burrow.
DraftKings has the Jaguars with the fourth-shortest odds to win the AFC (+590), behind the Ravens (+390), Bills (+395) and Chiefs (+405). The Jaguars probably belong among those teams, but not as the definitive favorite. It's a crowded group, and that doesn't even include the Broncos or Patriots.Two things can be true: The Jaguars look like the best team in the AFC right now, and I'm not sure I would take them as my pick to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl at the moment.Still, it's absurd how much they're being overlooked. Only the 49ers have a better line-of-scrimmage expected points added, and they've played a much easier schedule. This is a really, really good team.
The Packers are back on track for playoff contentionOverreaction or reality: OverreactionThe Packers eked out a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers to get to 2-2 on the season, but major problems persist.Jordan Love threw an awful interception late in the game that gave the Buccaneers life.Kaleb Johnson had a red zone fumble.The rushing game was better — a season-high 40% rushing success rate — but still not good. Factor in the Johnson fumble, and the Packers still had a -0.25 EPA per rush.The Buccaneers, playing with an undrafted rookie backup quarterback, posted a 54% rushing success rate and racked up 141 rushing yards.And in new negative developments, CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reports that the Packers fear standout linebacker Edgerrin Cooper has torn his Achilles.The biggest positive for Green Bay (after winning the game, of course) was that Love took no sacks. The offensive line was much better. But this team is still miles away from looking like a playoff contender, and that goes for both sides of the ball.
Ben Johnson will win Coach of the YearOverreaction or reality: OverreactionBen Johnson should be the frontrunner for Coach of the Year. He's now won games with Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum ... and it's only Week 4! According to CBS Sports research, only one other team has had three different quarterbacks throw for 200+ yards in a win through four weeks: the 1997 Jaguars.Unfortunately for Johnson's Coach of the Year candidacy, the award tends to go to a coach whose team way overachieves: Mike Vrabel's Patriots last year, Kevin O'Connell's Vikings (with Sam Darnold) in 2024, Kevin Stefanski's Browns in 2023, Brian Daboll's Giants in 2022.Basically, the external preseason expectations were likely too high for Johnson and the Bears for him to win the award this year, even if you could argue he's been the best coach in the sport so far. 
Dan Quinn belongs on the hot seatOverreaction or reality: RealityThere are a lot of things Dan Quinn cannot control. He can't control that Jayden Daniels is hurt, nor that Marcus Mariota got hurt Sunday, forcing the Commanders to turn to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis under center. He cannot control that the team has injuries pretty much everywhere up and down the roster. He can't control a litany of other problems, including that there simply isn't enough talent, period.But the things he can control aren't going his way, either. The biggest mistake in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts in London was going for a fourth-and-1 in his own territory late in the first half. At the time, the Commanders were leading 6-0. The defense was dominant, forcing two Daniel Jones turnovers. A punt would have been the easy answer, especially with a third-string rookie at quarterback.Instead, the Commanders failed on a mess of a play, giving the Colts the spark they needed. Indianapolis scored a touchdown and never trailed again.Washington is also one of the most penalized teams in the NFL. Now 1-3 with a ton of tough matchups upcoming, the Commanders face a must-win against the Giants in Week 5.The Dolphins won't win a game this seasonOverreaction or reality: OverreactionWe won't forget about you, Dolphins. I promise!Miami fell to 0-4 with a 15-10 loss to the Vikings. It was a mostly unsightly game, with Brian Flores' defense wreaking havoc. But the Dolphins got plenty of good moments, including this bittersweet one:
Also positive for the Dolphins?Ollie Gordon II: 9 carries, 100 yards, one touchdownJacob Rodriguez: 18 tacklesFour sacks, including two by Zach Sieler, one of the NFL's most underrated playersLots of young guys look good, which is what matters most.Is this a missed opportunity for a win? Sure. But small misses are way better than big misses. Miami will win a game this year.
